name: beccs_capex_premium
description: Increase in total CAPEX for post-combustion capture and compression relative to BES at equal thermal input
notes: IEAGHG (2009) dedicated biomass CFB/BFB: +38-40% total investment (+114-126% per kWe net); range spans co-fired cases (+25-30%) to the upper end of Bhave et al. (2017).

name: beccs_eff_penalty
description: BECCS efficiency penalty (percentage points below BES)

name: capture_rate
description: BECCS CO2 capture efficiency
notes: Validation needed: Real-world data is sparse. Recommend sensitivity analysis (85-95%).

name: ccs_distance
description: CCS transport distance

name: co2_pipeline_terrain_share
description: Fraction of CO2 pipeline CAPEX that scales with the route-average terrain cost multiplier (v2 transport layers)
notes: 1 = multiplier applies to all pipeline CAPEX, as terrain factors are usually quoted (IEA 2002); lower if unit costs already include a terrain allowance.

name: co2_subsea_capex_factor
description: Subsea CO2 pipeline CAPEX per km relative to onshore (offshore sinks reached by pipeline)
notes: Offshore pipelines typically cost 1.4-1.7x onshore per km. Keep equal to sea_route_weight_pipe in data-raw/process_transport_layers.R, which uses it to choose the landfall.

name: ccs_storage_cost
description: Onshore injection and monitoring (exploration to post-closure), for sinks without a site-specific cost
notes: Global CCS Institute (2025), 2024 USD: onshore US$2-15/t (open boundary), 5-33 (moderate closed), up to 58; ZEP (2011) onshore saline EUR 2-12/t.

name: cost_offshore_storage
description: Offshore injection and monitoring (exploration to post-closure), for sinks without a site-specific cost
notes: Global CCS Institute (2025), 2024 USD: offshore US$5-31/t (open boundary), 8-50 (moderate closed), up to 147; ZEP (2011) offshore saline EUR 6-20/t.

name: storage_cost_factor
description: Multiplier on site-specific CO2 storage costs (classified sinks in co2_sinks)
notes: Sinks with a site-specific cost (NETL formation cost for US onshore saline; GCCSI open or closed saline; ZEP depleted field) use Storage_Cost in co2_sinks x this factor. Range spans the NETL all-optimistic / all-pessimistic sensitivity (0.74-1.35 for Mount Simon, 0.57-1.71 for Copper Ridge) and most of the GCCSI and ZEP within-class ranges (issue #103).

name: co2_ship_emis_fixed
description: CO2 emitted per tonne shipped, fixed part (liquefaction, loading, intermediate storage)
notes: From Al Baroudi et al. (2021): emissions of liquefaction and electricity are ~2.5% of CO2 transported at 200 km and ~18% at 12,000 km (fixed ~2.2% + 0.0013%/km).

name: co2_ship_emis_per_km
description: CO2 emitted per tonne shipped per km of voyage
notes: Al Baroudi et al. (2021); see co2_ship_emis_fixed. Pipeline lift pumping electricity is counted at the displaced grid intensity.

name: bes_capital_cost
description: Local CAPEX for BES at a 50 MWe reference plant (quoted at bes_capex_ref_eff); already regional, so capex_location_factor is not applied
notes: US: EIA AEO2026 (Sargent & Lundy) 50 MW wood BFB $4,843/kW 2025$ = ~4,720 (AEO2020: $4,097 2019$ = 5,030). Europe: Danish Energy Agency (2020) large straw CHP, 41.6 MWe, EUR 3.4M/MWe 2015 (range 2.9-4.0) = 4,990, ~4,720 scaled to 50 MWe; divided by 1.09 (DEA straw vs wood-chip CHP cost per MW fuel input, 80 MW feed plants) = ~4,330, because the base is a wood-fired plant and the ash penalty (adjust_costs_for_fuel) is added separately; cf. DEA medium wood-chip CHP scaled to 50 MWe ~4,110. China and India: IRENA (2025) weighted-average installed cost of bioenergy commissioned in 2024, 2,180 and 1,858 (2024 USD). India low end: CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024 rice-straw Rankine norm Rs 697 lakh/MW = ~925/kWe net, so India's lower bound is 0.5 (950). Range otherwise x0.85-1.25, covering the DEA 2020 range and AEO2020.

name: bes_capex_ref_eff
description: Net electrical efficiency at which bes_capital_cost is quoted; sizes combustion CAPEX from thermal input
notes: Fixed design point, so sampled efficiency, ash and CCS penalties change output but not equipment cost.

name: bes_energy_efficiency
description: Electrical efficiency for BES
notes: Danish Energy Agency (2026), Technology Data for Electricity and District Heating Production: ~30% net electrical efficiency for biomass condensing plants.

name: avail_k
description: First-year potassium availability

name: avail_n
description: First-year nitrogen availability

name: avail_p
description: First-year phosphorus availability

name: bc_ag_value
description: Biochar agronomic value

name: bc_cce
description: Calcium Carbonate Equivalent
notes: Validation needed: Does 15% hold true globally, or should it scale with bm_ash?

name: bc_cec_value
description: Annual crop-yield benefit of biochar from raising soil CEC, at CEC <= 5 cmol/kg, falling linearly to 0 at CEC >= 30; valued as a perpetuity, annual value / (discount rate + biochar C decay rate)
notes: Woolf, Lehmann & Lee (2016) Nat. Commun. 7, 13160: mean crop-yield benefit 30 $/Mg C/yr (2008-2013 average price basis), of which about half is attributable to CEC (the rest to pH, credited separately as a lime substitute) = 15; x1.409 (US CPI-U 2024 / mean 2008-2013) = 21.1. Perpetuity because biochar CEC rises with ageing; the decay rate is -ln(Fperm)/100. Range is a judgement.

name: ash_cce
description: Calcium carbonate equivalent of recycled combustion ash
notes: Default set for alkalinity mass balance with bc_cce at default feedstock ash and biochar yield.

name: ash_p_content
description: Phosphorus content of recycled combustion ash (elemental P)
notes: Default set for P mass balance with bc_p_content at default feedstock ash and biochar yield.

name: bc_k_content
description: Biochar potassium content (elemental K)

name: bc_n_content
description: Biochar Nitrogen content

name: bc_p_content
description: Biochar phosphorus content (elemental P)

name: bc_price
description: Biochar price

name: bc_stab_factor
description: Biochar stability factor
notes: Validation needed: Ensure aligns with IPCC or verified carbon standard methodologies.

name: n_app_rate
description: Mineral N fertiliser application rate on cropland
notes: FAOSTAT N use per ha of cropland (via Our World in Data), 2019-2023 mean; default = world mean.

name: n2o_ef
description: Direct N2O emission factor for fertiliser N
notes: IPCC (2019) Refinement EF1 aggregated default and uncertainty range.

name: n2o_reduction
description: Fractional reduction in soil N2O emissions after biochar application
notes: Woolf et al. (2021): 23% reduction (95% CI 5-41%) in field trials with >10 Mg C/ha biochar.

name: n2o_years
description: Duration of biochar N2O reduction
notes: Significant effects demonstrated only in the first year (Woolf et al. 2021); long tail reflects uncertainty.

name: bc_app_rate_c
description: Biochar application rate for N2O effect
notes: Minimum application for which Woolf et al. (2021) credit N2O reduction.

name: bc_field_cost
description: Biochar field application cost (spreading and incorporation)
notes: nets1.xlsm (Woolf et al. 2016) bc_field_cost: central 87.8, range 0-175.6 $/ha, converted from 2014 to 2024 USD (x1.325; base year to confirm). Per Mg biochar at the application rate bc_app_rate_c / biochar C content; scaled by haulage_location_factor.

name: bc_field_diesel
description: Tractor diesel use for biochar spreading and incorporation
notes: Median of four estimates for spreading and incorporation: Roberts et al. (2010) 506 MJ/ha = ~13 L/ha; Cheng et al. (2025) tillage ~15 L/ha; Leppakoski et al. (2021) manure spreader 14 + power harrow 6 = 20 L/ha; Pujol Pereira et al. (2016) 220 L/ha (orchard, 12.2 h/ha tractor time). Range 13 (lowest estimate) to 30 (Cheng et al. tillage plus planting); the orchard value is excluded from the range as unrepresentative of broadacre fields. 2.68 kg CO2/L.

name: price_k
description: Market price for potassium (world market; all regions)
notes: Potassium chloride 516 $/t / 0.60 kg K2O/kg. World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), annual nominal prices 2021-2025, each year escalated to 2024 USD with US CPI-U, then averaged. World market price used in all regions: retail subsidies (India) and export controls (China) are transfers that do not reduce the economic value of the fertilizer displaced.

name: price_lime
description: Cost of agricultural lime delivered and spread, per Mg of calcium carbonate equivalent (100% ECCE)
notes: Median of literature values incl. transport and application, converted to 100% ECCE and escalated with US CPI-U: Latawiec et al. (2019) Brazil 24.7 $/t delivered, no application (2018) = 31; Mills et al. (2020) Oklahoma (9.92 lime + 5.51 transport + 7.72 application) / 0.55 ECCE (2019) = 52 (Mills et al. 2023 use the same prices); Cho et al. (2020) Oklahoma 48 near / 90 far from quarry at 100% ECCE incl. application (2019) = 59 / 110; Woods et al. (2026) North Carolina 85 $/t spread (USDA, Dec 2024). Price years assumed one year before publication where not stated.

name: price_n
description: Market price for nitrogen (world market; all regions)
notes: Urea 486 $/t / 0.46 kg N/kg. World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), annual nominal prices 2021-2025, each year escalated to 2024 USD with US CPI-U, then averaged. World market price used in all regions: retail subsidies (India) and export controls (China) are transfers that do not reduce the economic value of the fertilizer displaced.

name: price_p
description: Market price for phosphorus (world market; all regions)
notes: Triple superphosphate 585 $/t / 0.46 kg P2O5/kg (a P-only fertilizer; DAP net of its N value gives 1.03). World Bank Commodity Price Data (Pink Sheet), annual nominal prices 2021-2025, each year escalated to 2024 USD with US CPI-U, then averaged. World market price used in all regions: retail subsidies (India) and export controls (China) are transfers that do not reduce the economic value of the fertilizer displaced.

name: py_cc
description: Pyrolysis unit capital cost at the base location (scaled by capex_location_factor), per Mg/yr of feed at the 50 MWe reference size
notes: Set so that the US value (x1.25) is 335: NREL, Yadav & Lamers (2026) Energy Fuels 40, 4670, slow pyrolysis 2000 dry t/day, nth-plant TCI $128M (2020$) = 195 $/(t/yr) at 90% on-stream (657 kt/yr) = 236 (2024$, CPI-U x1.212), scaled with exponent 0.7 to the 206 kt/yr reference = 335. Other regions follow capex_location_factor (Europe 308, China 188, India 174). Caveat: NREL reactor at 300 C (model 500 C).

name: py_life
description: Pyrolysis project lifetime
notes: Woolf et al. (2016) Nature Communications (nets1 model).

name: bebcs_power_life
description: BEBCS power block lifetime
notes: Woolf et al. (2016) Nature Communications (nets1 model).

name: bebcs_heat_life
description: BEBCS heat block lifetime

name: bebcs_power_capital_cost
description: Pyrolysis vapour/gas combustion and steam power block capital cost at the base location (scaled by capex_location_factor)
notes: Set so that the US value (x1.25) is 3,250: between the steam cycle alone, 2,650 (Dutta et al. 2015, NREL/TP-5100-62455 / PNNL-23823, nth plant: steam system and power generation TIC $52.45M for 48.3 MWe x FCI/TIC 1.747 = 1,897 $/kWe 2011$, x1.395 CPI-U), and a complete 50 MW biomass plant including solid-fuel handling (4,700; EIA AEO2026); the midpoint of a 3,000-3,500 range allows for the vapour/gas combustor and boiler. Range 2,600-4,060 (US). Other regions follow capex_location_factor.

name: bebcs_heat_capital_cost
description: Syngas heat generation capital cost

name: bebcs_heat_efficiency
description: Heat-only block efficiency (heat sold / fuel LHV; heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: Biomass/syngas boiler for process heat; TODO(#106) source.

name: heat_price
description: No-carbon price of the displaced heat (fuel cost / boiler efficiency; heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: Exploratory, TODO(#106) source: US delivered industrial gas ~4.5 $/MMBtu / 0.9 = 17; EU TTF 2024 ~34 EUR/MWh / 0.9 = 41; China thermal coal ~850 CNY/t / 0.8 = 23; India domestic coal / 0.75 = 15.

name: heat_boiler_ci
description: Life-cycle intensity of the fossil boiler heat displaced (heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: Exploratory, TODO(#106) source: gas boiler (US, Europe) ~0.20 combustion + upstream / 0.9 = 0.25; coal boiler (China, India) ~0.34 / 0.8 + upstream = 0.45. Displaced heat intensity = min(boiler, MEF(P) / heat_pump_cop).

name: heat_pump_cop
description: Seasonal COP of the grid heat pump that displaced heat converges to as the grid decarbonises
notes: Typical air- or ground-source heat pump seasonal COP for low- and medium-temperature heat.

name: heat_offtake
description: Share of heat output sold (heat sensitivity scenario)
notes: 1 = year-round heat demand at the plant; the scenario is reported only conditionally on such demand existing.

name: py_temp
description: Peak pyrolysis temperature
notes: Modelling assumption: the medium pyrolysis temperature class (450-600 C) of Woolf et al. (2021) Environ. Sci. Technol. 55, 14795-14805 and IPCC (2019) Refinement Vol. 4 Ch. 2 Appendix 4. Sampled to represent imperfect temperature control and gradients within the reactor and particles; drives biochar yield and H:C (permanence) jointly.

name: py_heater_eff
description: Pyrolysis process heater efficiency (HHV basis)
notes: Woolf et al. (2014) Environ. Sci. Technol. 48, 6492-6499.

name: py_parasitic_power
description: Pyrolysis plant parasitic electricity demand
notes: Woolf et al. (2014) Environ. Sci. Technol. 48, 6492-6499.

name: py_exhaust_temp
description: Temperature of vapours and gases leaving heat recovery

name: bebcs_power_efficiency
description: Electrical efficiency of pyrolysis fuel power block (LHV basis)
notes: Woolf et al. (2014) Environ. Sci. Technol. 48, 6492-6499.

name: target_ph
description: Target agricultural soil pH

name: time_frame
description: Time horizon of pyC permanence

name: gj_to_mwh
description: Conversion factor from GJ to MWh

name: gwp_n2o
description: Global warming potential of N2O (100-yr)
notes: IPCC AR6.

name: gwp_ch4
description: Global warming potential of non-fossil CH4 (100-yr)
notes: IPCC AR6.

name: kg_to_mg
description: Conversion factor from kg to Mg

name: molar_ratio_co2_c
description: Molar ratio of CO2 to C

name: allow_eor
description: Allow Enhanced Oil Recovery

name: ash_recycling
description: Recycle BES/BECCS combustion ash to cropland (lime and P value)

name: bc_return_haul
description: Charge handling for returning biochar to fields as a backhaul in the feedstock trucks

name: py_e_source
description: Pyrolysis process energy source (fuel / biomass / biochar)

name: bc_valuation_method
description: Biochar valuation method

name: beccs_available
description: Is BECCS available

name: early_adoption
description: BECCS early adoption scenario

name: optimize_scale
description: Optimize plant scale

name: sink_is_offshore
description: Is the CO2 sink offshore?

name: use_flat_ci
description: Use a flat displaced carbon intensity (flat_ci_tCO2_GJ; e.g. nuclear, 12 g/kWh) instead of the price-dependent MEF(P)
notes: Control option only; not used in sensitivity or MC.

name: mef_price_dependent
description: Scale each cell's empirical build margin with the NGFS-fitted MEF(P) curve at the scenario carbon price
notes: FALSE = static empirical build margin (pre-MEF behaviour).

name: mef_include_remind
description: Use the MEF(P) fit that includes REMIND-MAgPIE
notes: Default excludes REMIND: its decline is driven by time rather than price, failing the fit-quality and model-agreement checks.

name: bm_ash
description: Biomass ash mass fraction
notes: Phyllis2 (TNO): wheat straw and corn stover ~5% (US, Europe); rice straw ~15% (China, India).

name: bm_c
description: Biomass carbon mass fraction
notes: Phyllis2 (TNO): cereal straws, corn stover and rice straw, dry ash-free basis.

name: residue_soil_ghg_penalty
description: Net soil GHG penalty of removing residues (forgone SOC minus avoided soil N2O)
notes: Default 0: McClelland et al. (2025) find the SOC gain and N2O increase from residue retention approximately cancel through 2100 in all regions studied except the Brazilian Cerrado. For sensitivity, a SOC-only penalty (no N2O offset) is bm_c x 0.11 x 44/12 = 0.19 (formerly residue_c_retention = 0.11).

name: residue_burn_fraction
description: Share of removed residues that would otherwise be burned in the field (regional fallback where residue_burn_map is absent)
notes: Superseded by the cell-level layer residue_burn_map (data-raw/generate_residue_burn_layer.R, issue #31): Smerald et al. (2023) cereal burnt / production share, 2017-2021, times SPAM cereal field residue C (Karan et al. 2023 inputs), divided by Karan et al. (2023) available residue C, capped at 1. Regional values are the biomass-weighted means of that layer. Earlier values: US 0.02 and China 0.10 (estimates), India 0.16 (Jain et al. 2014, share of all residues generated), Europe 0.01 (EU burning ban).

name: residue_burn_factor
description: Multiplier on the cell-level burnt share (residue_burn_map)
notes: Uncertainty in the burnt share: satellite fire products under-detect small field fires (e.g. Punjab), and burning of non-cereal residues is not counted; the product is capped at 1.

name: residue_burn_cf
description: Combustion factor for field burning of residues
notes: IPCC (2006) Vol. 4 Table 2.6.

name: residue_burn_ch4_ef
description: CH4 emission factor for field burning of residues
notes: IPCC (2006) Vol. 4 Table 2.5.

name: residue_burn_n2o_ef
description: N2O emission factor for field burning of residues
notes: IPCC (2006) Vol. 4 Table 2.5.

name: bm_h
description: Biomass hydrogen mass fraction (daf)

name: bm_h2o
description: Biomass moisture content

name: bm_lhv
description: Biomass lower heating value (dry ash-free)
notes: Phyllis2 (TNO): cereal straws, corn stover and rice straw, dry ash-free basis.

name: bm_transport_fixed
description: Fixed loading/handling cost
notes: Beach et al. (2012): loading and handling 4.59 $/dry t (2012 USD) x 1.366 (US CPI-U 2024/2012). Also charged per Mg of biochar returned to fields as a backhaul.

name: bm_transport_var
description: Variable trucking cost per km of one-way haul (includes the empty return)
notes: Searcy et al. (2007): truck distance-variable cost 0.12 $/Mg/km for straw and stover in 2006 USD; x1.556 (US CPI-U 2006 to 2024) = 0.187, rounded to 0.19 in 2024 USD. Check: US truck operating cost ~$1.4 per km travelled (ATRI 2024) / 18-20 t payload x 2 for the empty return = ~0.15 $/t per one-way km.

name: feedstock_storage_cost
description: Interim storage of seasonally harvested residues for year-round supply (about six months), US/EU basis; scaled by haulage_location_factor
notes: Literature spread (2024 USD/Mg, dry): Becerra-Perez et al. (2022) 3.1; Brechbill & Tyner (2008) 6.9; Beach et al. (2012) FASOMGHG 10.5 at 4.6 months, 11.1 at 6 months ($1.00 fixed + $4.59 in/out + $0.30/month per dry ton); Shackley et al. (2011) UK on-farm 18 (26 weeks at $0.50/t/week), purpose-built 31; Kung et al. (2013) 34 (storage and handling); Karras & Thran (2024) Germany ~42 (36.4% of supply cost at 6 months, 86% dm). Central 15 between the US farm-scale estimates and UK on-farm storage; range spans the literature. Regional values via haulage_location_factor: US 15, Europe 15, China 11.3, India 9.8 (cf. CEEW India: storage 20-30% of delivered cost, ~7-10). Ebadian et al. (2013): dedicated loading equipment at storage sites is costly (used 3-11% of the year).

name: india_feedstock_cost
description: Field-side price of baled paddy straw in India, dry basis (used for India only; other regions use calculate_regional_feedstock_cost() values)
notes: Sokhansanj et al. (2023) J. Sustain. Bioenergy Syst. 13, 57: baled straw $33.14/t dm (2023 USD) x 1.029 = 34. Range: Erenstein (2011) paddy straw Rs 0.31/kg (~2008) = ~12, where straw is burned, to fodder-market straw ~50: rice straw Rs 246/100 kg, Patna (Duncan et al. 2020); wheat residue Rs 332.5/quintal (Lopes et al. 2023); maize stover Rs 3,000/t (Varatharajan et al. 2022). Pant & Pant (2025): rice straw $40-60/t potential farmer income. Replaces Rs 1,600/t (trade news).

name: haul_time_share
description: Share of variable trucking cost that is time-based (driver wages and benefits; truck payments; insurance; permits)
notes: ATRI (2024) An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking: 2024 Update (2023 cost per mile). Scaled by the travel-time factor haul_kt.

name: haul_fuel_share
description: Share of variable trucking cost that is fuel
notes: ATRI (2024). Scaled by road distance and climb (haul_kd x haul_g); the remainder (repairs; tyres; tolls) scales with road distance.

name: lignin
description: Lignin fraction

name: transport_emissions_factor
description: Heavy-duty truck emissions

name: bes_life
description: BES (and BECCS) plant lifetime
notes: Danish Energy Agency (2026), Technology Data for Electricity and District Heating Production: 25-year technical lifetime for biomass power and CHP plants.

name: c_price
description: Carbon abatement credit price

name: capacity_factor
description: Annual plant capacity utilization (levelised: output / maximum output)
notes: Rubin (2012): levelised capacity factors of US base-load plants 0.65-0.75 (median 0.70). The DEA (2026) availability of 0.91 counts only planned and unplanned outages, not part-load operation.

name: discount_rate
description: Cost of capital (real, after-tax WACC for bioenergy projects)
notes: Hatton et al. (2025) Sci. Data 12, 1912 bioenergy WACC projected for 2030 (nominal, post-tax, USD): US 8.2%, EU-27 mean 9.45%, China 8.9%, India 9.8%; converted to real with 2.5% expected USD inflation: (1 + n)/1.025 - 1. Real because all cash flows are in constant 2024 USD. After-tax (the common TEA convention); a pre-tax gross-up at statutory corporate tax rates (Tax Foundation 2024) would give 8.3/9.3/9.1/11.2% but overstates the effective tax wedge, which depreciation allowances reduce. Default = US.

name: capex_location_factor
description: Regional multiplier on CAPEX quoted on a US/EU basis (pyrolysis, BEBCS energy block, CO2 pipelines, liquefaction and terminals); not applied to BES/BECCS, whose CAPEX is set regionally
notes: Applied in code to base CAPEX values.

name: plant_om_factor
description: Annual O&M (fixed + variable) as a fraction of total CAPEX, for all conversion plants (BES, BECCS, pyrolysis, BEBCS energy block)
notes: EIA AEO2023 50 MW biomass: fixed $141.5/kW-yr + $5.44/MWh = 3.6%/yr at 85% capacity factor; IRENA (2012) stoker/BFB/CFB boilers: fixed 3.2-4.2% + $3.8-4.7/MWh; Danish Energy Agency technology data, 80 MW feed CHP: straw 4.4%, wood pellets 4.6%/yr all-in.

name: om_location_factor
description: Regional multiplier on the O&M-to-CAPEX fraction
notes: 1 everywhere: regional CAPEX already scales O&M in absolute terms. Evidence: EIA AEO2026 and DEA (2020) all-in O&M ~4.1% of CAPEX/yr; CERC (India, 2024) O&M Rs 54.7 lakh/MW/yr = 7.8% of its normative CAPEX, so lower labour cost does not lower the O&M-to-CAPEX ratio.

name: haulage_location_factor
description: Regional multiplier on biomass haulage costs
notes: Relative road-freight costs; India ~0.047 USD/t-km vs ~0.07 USD/t-km for US/EU truckload.

name: elec_price
description: Wholesale electricity price received by the plant (scalar fallback; spatial runs use the regional price layer)
notes: Spatial runs use data-raw/generate_elec_price_layer.R: wholesale (day-ahead or hub) prices averaged over 2023-2025, from EIA STEO hub prices (US), Ember/ENTSO-E day-ahead prices (Europe), provincial coal benchmark tariffs excl. VAT (China) and IEX day-ahead prices (India). The Monte Carlo range is applied as a multiplier on the layer.

name: ff_c_intensity
description: Displaced grid carbon intensity at today's effective carbon price (empirical build margin, IPCC life-cycle, biomass = 0)
notes: Spatial layer (generate_marginal_ci.R); scaled by MEF(P) at the scenario carbon price.

name: grid_p_now
description: Current explicit carbon price on power-sector emissions (MEF(P) anchor)
notes: 2024 averages: EU ETS EUR 65/t x 1.08 USD/EUR = 70; China national ETS CNY 98/t / 7.20 CNY/USD = 14; no national price in the US or India. The TEA carbon price is an explicit price.

name: mef_floor
description: Residual life-cycle intensity of a decarbonised grid (MEF(P) floor)
notes: Pehl et al. (2017): 2050 life-cycle emissions of nuclear, wind and solar 3.5-12 g/kWh; fossil CCS 78-110 g/kWh.

name: mef_draw_u
description: Selects a bootstrap draw of the MEF(P) curve (0 = central fit)
notes: Monte Carlo: uniform on (0, 1] picks one of 1,000 precomputed bootstrap draws (inst/extdata/mef_shape_draws.csv).

name: flat_ci_tCO2_GJ
description: Flat carbon intensity value

name: plant_sizes_mw_th
description: Available plant sizes

name: rebound
description: Rebound effect

name: scaling_factor
description: Capital cost scale exponent

name: avg_dist
description: Average collection distance

name: collection_radius
description: Collection radius

name: dist_offshore
description: Distance to offshore sink

name: dist_onshore
description: Distance to onshore sink

name: dist_sink_km
description: Distance to EOR sink

name: dist_sink_saline_km
description: Distance to saline sink

name: feedstock_cost
description: Feedstock purchase cost

name: soil_cec
description: Cation Exchange Capacity

name: soil_ph
description: Native topsoil pH

name: soil_temp
description: Mean annual soil temperature

name: tortuosity
description: Road tortuosity factor

name: plant_mw_th
description: Target plant thermal capacity
